S0.title: I²S microphone
S0.heading: Read and hear the ICS-43434 on J20
S0.goal: Connect the ICS-43434 to the six-pin J20 connector. Read its I²S peak in the serial console, then stream PCM over USB Serial/JTAG and listen in the browser. Both MicroPython scripts open in this exercise's Code view.
S0.goalLine: Check the microphone level, then hear the same J20 microphone in the browser.
goalCheck: The console prints Audio peak (24-bit): with a changing value when you speak.
The browser listener receives PCM frames, changes its signal state and plays your voice.
The listening gain changes playback volume while dBFS keeps reporting the original samples.

wiring.title: Connect J20 directly to the ICS-43434 J1 connector
head: Board J20
ICS-43434 J1
Signal
rows: Drive low to select the left channel

steps: Install the included MicroPython preview firmware at 0x0000 from Flash firmware. It includes machine.I2S.
Unplug USB and connect the six J20 pins to the ICS-43434 J1 pins in the same order. Plug USB back in; J20 is not the four-pin Qwiic connector.
Open Code, connect the serial console and run mic_ics43434_j20.py. Speak near the microphone and watch the peak change.
Stop the script, select mic_ics43434_usb_master.py and run it. In the listening dialog, press Listen to hear the microphone in the browser.
Adjust Listening gain if playback is quiet. If it distorts, lower the gain. Press Stop listening before leaving the exercise.
S0.note: Do not use the microSD card while listening to the J20 I²S microphone: both use GPIO27, GPIO7 and GPIO26. SPI card activity can interfere with I²S and cause audible clicks. The listener detects valid PCM and signal level, not the microphone's electrical identity. A silent or disconnected module may look the same. Listening gain does not change the incoming PCM or dBFS reading.

S1.title: ES8311 microphone
S1.heading: Hear the ES8311 microphone
S1.goal: Connect the ES8311 codec and capture the analog microphone on its J2 input through the codec ADC. Check the level in the serial console, then stream the samples over USB and listen in the browser.
S1.goalLine: See a changing peak level, then hear your voice in the browser.
goalCheck: The capture script prints a changing peak level when you speak into the analog microphone.
The browser receives the codec's PCM stream and plays your voice.
The listening gain changes playback volume while dBFS keeps reporting the original samples.

steps: Install the included MicroPython preview firmware at 0x0000 from Flash firmware. It includes machine.I2S.

Unplug USB and wire the codec as shown above. DOUT goes to the exposed D6/GPIO24 pad, outside J20; leave DIN connected too, the speaker exercises use it. Connect an analog microphone to the codec's J2 input, then reconnect USB.
Open Code, connect the serial console and use Install es8311.py to save the codec driver on the board.
Run es8311_mic_capture.py and speak near the microphone. Watch the frames per second and peak level in the console; use es8311_mic_diagnose.py if the input stays silent.
Stop the capture script and run es8311_mic_usb_audio.py. Press Listen in the audio dialog to hear the microphone in the browser. Adjust Listening gain if needed, then press Stop listening.
S1.note: The microphone path uses DOUT on D6/GPIO24, BCLK, WS and MCLK on J20, and I²C on QWIIC for configuration. Listening gain changes the browser speaker only; the PCM samples and dBFS reading stay unchanged. Avoid using the microSD card while J20 carries I²S audio, because the shared GPIOs can cause interference.

Run es8311_sound_clap.py. In the panel, raise sensitivity if the peak does not cross the displayed threshold.

S3.note: The detector uses 16 ms blocks. Some knocks or sharp sounds can also trigger it; the web switch does not control a physical load.

S7.title: ES8311 speaker
S7.heading: Play tones and songs through the ES8311
S7.goal: Drive the ES8311 DAC and amplifier from MicroPython: play a melody, shape a tone while it sounds, then stream a song from the browser to the speaker.
S7.goalLine: Hear a melody, change a tone live, then play a song from the browser.
goalCheck: The melody script plays notes through the speaker connected to the ES8311 module.
The tone lab changes pitch, waveform and level while the ES8311 plays through the speaker.
The music player changes codec volume while an included song is playing.

steps: Connect the analog microphone to the ES8311 J2 input. With USB unplugged, connect the codec as shown above, then reconnect USB. Install the included MicroPython firmware from Flash firmware and save es8311.py to the board from Code.
Connect a speaker to the codec amplifier output. Run es8311_melody.py to hear a short melody.

Stop the melody, select es8311_tone_lab.py and run it. The tone panel opens automatically. Hold a note or press Play tone; change frequency, waveform and level, then press Silence. You can reopen the panel with Open tone lab.

Stop the tone lab, select es8311_play_serial.py and run it. In the audio player, choose one of the three included songs or open your own WAV or MP3, pick a quality and press Play on the board. Raise or lower Volume while the song plays. The browser converts the song to mono and streams it over USB. Use Voice or Standard for the smoothest sound.
S7.note: Playback uses DIN on J20/GPIO26 with the same BCLK, WS and MCLK wires as the microphone. The C5 has one I²S peripheral, so run one script at a time. The player's volume changes the codec volume; the tone lab changes the level of the samples it generates.

S8.heading: Hear your voice with effects
S8.goal: Record two seconds of speech, then replay the same take through fourteen effects and a low, high or band pass filter with an adjustable cutoff.

Moving the cutoff changes the filter curve and what you hear.

steps: Connect the analog microphone to the ES8311 J2 input. With USB unplugged, connect the codec as shown above, then reconnect USB. Install the included MicroPython firmware from Flash firmware and save es8311.py to the board from Code.
Connect a speaker to the codec amplifier output. Run es8311_sound_voice_fx.py; the effects panel opens automatically.

Press Record and speak. Choose an effect, set its intensity, pick a filter and its cutoff, then press Play effect. The board processes the take first, then plays it. Try other settings with the same take.
S8.note: The board renders each effect into memory before playing it, so heavy effects never stutter; processing takes a moment. The microphone is off during playback, so it does not hear its own speaker. Speed effects change both pitch and duration.
